releaseTrainNote: Declared 'mvp' to match the reasoned declaration already carried by this packet's own artifacts (spec.md section 'Release Train', and the headers of spec.md, report.md and scopes.md). This is NOT the train the two sibling specs authored in the same session chose. Specs 111 and 112 both chose 'next', and their recorded reason does not transfer: 111 chose 'next' because it introduces a fail-closed egress enforcement point whose grants are defined by spec 108, which is itself on 'next'; 112 chose 'next' because it RAISES reach while spec 108's per-capability authorization that would bound it is not yet delivered. Spec 110 introduces no authorization change at all — Non-Goal 1 states it changes what retrieval finds, never whose corpus it searches — and consumes nothing from spec 108. The security-posture argument that moved both siblings is therefore simply absent here, and copying it would be a borrowed justification rather than a real one. See executionHistory[1].releaseTrainRationale for the four grounds on which 'mvp' was affirmed on this spec's own merits, and for the honest cost of that choice.
flagsIntroducedNote: EMPTY by design, not by omission, and this DIVERGES from this packet's own spec.md, which is recorded rather than hidden. spec.md section 'Release Train' proposes the flag name `chunkedHybridRetrieval` and correctly states that the bundle edits are owned by bubbles.train. Verified on 2026-08-04 by repo-wide grep: `chunkedHybridRetrieval` occurs in exactly three places, all of them prose inside this spec folder (spec.md:449, spec.md:457, design.md:63). It is absent from config/feature-flags.mvp.yaml and absent from config/feature-flags.next.yaml, both of which currently declare only card_rewards and clientReleaseLaneB. Listing the flag here while no bundle carries it would produce a declaration that reads as configured and is enforced by nothing — the exact anti-pattern spec 111 named in its own flagsIntroducedNote. Note that release-train-guard.sh Check 8 would NOT have caught this: it errors only when a named flag is default-ON in a non-owning train, and an absent flag reads as 'unset' and passes. The declaration would therefore have been silently wrong rather than loudly wrong, which is a stronger reason to leave it empty. Routed to bubbles.train as F-110-FLAG-01. The flag must be declared in both bundles before SCOPE-02 or SCOPE-04 executes, because it is what decides which retrieval representation serves reads during the re-embed window.
planningOnlyNote: DELIBERATELY false, and this is a considered divergence from siblings 111 and 112 rather than an oversight. Both siblings set planningOnly:true because they are `product-to-planning` packets whose delivery is expected to happen later under a separate implementation spec (each carries plannedFixWorkflowMode:'full-delivery' and linkedImplementationSpec:null). Spec 110 is not shaped that way: spec.md, report.md and scopes.md all declare workflowMode `full-delivery`, and the five scopes in scopes.md are this spec's own delivery scopes, executed under this spec. It is its own implementation target. Setting planningOnly:true here would assert that this packet has no delivery target, which is false. G087 (planning-packet-implementation-linkage) enforces the linkage requirement only at status `specs_hardened`; this packet is `not_started`, so no linkage obligation is currently active.

outstandingFindings.summary: Changing the declared embedding model also changes the vector width (E5/E6: the declared model is not the 384-dimension one the column was sized for), so re-embedding is simultaneously a column-type migration on the corpus's largest table, with its own downtime, disk and rollback profile. The plan of record names re-embedding but does not name this. Sharpened by the mvp train choice: this migration lands on the live corpus, not on staging.

D1's two branches are both still open (E8: ivfflat probes never set; E9: no approximate-nearest-neighbour graph index exists — the single hnsw match in the repository is a test-fixture sentence, not an index). Which branch is true determines whether this is primarily an accuracy fix or primarily a latency fix, and therefore what the first measured floors even mean. Nothing may declare a floor before this is executed.

E12 shows the precedent failure is still live: tests/eval/assistant/acceptance_test.go carries a //go:build integration tag and ./tests/eval/... is absent from the integration lane's package list, so an existing gate whose thresholds the SST calls non-negotiable executes in no lane. Adding this spec's gate to the same directory without fixing the lane would ship a second gate that never runs. Whether the fix is extending the existing lane or declaring a new named one is a design call.

R-110-18 requires floors to come from measurement, but the first run has no prior measurement to compare against. The first execution is therefore baseline-establishing, not gating, and that transition must be an explicit recorded step or the first green run will be mistaken for a passed gate.

NFR-110-3 forbids using a real user corpus, but a vague query with a known answer is only meaningful against content rich enough to be ambiguous. Authoring 100+ genuinely vague cases over synthetic content is real work and is trivially under-scoped into 100 keyword lookups, which would measure nothing.

Passages persist a second copy of raw user content in a new location, so every existing rule about content handling, retention, export and deletion must extend to it or portability and deletion silently become incomplete. Interacts directly with spec 111's manifest record classes.

R-110-04 requires indexing actual content while constraint C110-4 retains a summary-vector signal in the fusion. Whether the summary vector remains a distinct signal or becomes redundant once passages exist is unresolved, and keeping a redundant signal would add cost without evidence of benefit.

Product Principle 2 states the metric as >75% correct on first result for vague queries. Whether that number becomes the declared accuracy@1 floor, or whether the measured baseline is lower and the gap is recorded honestly, is a product decision — not one the gate should make by adopting whatever it first measures.

executionHistory.releaseTrainRationale: Affirmed `mvp` (config/release-trains.yaml id: mvp, phase: active, target_slot: home-lab, flags_bundle: config/feature-flags.mvp.yaml) on this spec's own merits, after testing whether the siblings' reasoning transfers. IT DOES NOT. Spec 111 chose `next` because it introduces a fail-closed egress enforcement point whose grant vocabulary is defined by spec 108, which is itself on `next`; spec 112 chose `next` because it raises reach while the per-capability authorization that would bound it is undelivered. Spec 110 introduces NO authorization change whatsoever — Non-Goal 1 states it changes what retrieval finds, never whose corpus it searches — and consumes nothing from spec 108. There is no security posture here that could be split across two trains, so the argument that moved both siblings is absent, and importing it would have been a borrowed justification. Four grounds support `mvp`. (1) This is a correctness fix to a promise the live train ALREADY MAKES: Product Principle 2's stated contract is >75% correct on first result for vague queries, it is ratified and BLOCKING, and spec.md section 3 establishes that no executed measurement of it exists anywhere in the repository. A fix to a shipped promise belongs on the train that shipped it. (2) The failure mode — a user cannot find a fact they saved — is being experienced on `mvp` today; deferring it to staging defers the user's relief, not the risk. (3) There is no hard dependency on a `next`-train spec. F-110-EGRESS-01 routes passage portability to spec 111, but that is a routed follow-on, not a prerequisite: all five scopes can execute without any artifact spec 111 produces. (4) The plan of record places P8 in Stage 4 on the critical path with Pillars A and C both depending on it, so holding it on staging stalls two dependent pillars. THE HONEST COST, stated rather than obscured by the train choice, is twofold and is recorded as findings rather than as reassurance. First, F-110-DIM-01: re-embedding is simultaneously a column-width migration on the corpus's largest table, and choosing `mvp` means that migration lands on the LIVE corpus — mitigated by the gating flag and by the resumability hard constraint in the outcome contract, but not eliminated, which is why F-110-DIM-01 is BLOCKING on bubbles.design before any scope executes. Second, F-110-TRAIN-01: passages add a second content-bearing copy of user data to the live train while spec 111, which covers its export and deletion, targets `next` — so Principle 11's unconditional-exit guarantee is weakened on the live train for the interval between the two promotions.
